_meta.source: MOE Full SBB pages and FAQ, MOE S1 posting pages, SEAB SEC pages, MOE PSE pages and press releases (2024 to 2026), school subject combination booklets as examples only
_meta.notes: Read from search engine extracts of the primary pages on 2026-10-27. Items marked provisional come from school booklets or secondary summaries and vary by school. Schools set their own review criteria and dates; the school's own are the real ones.

p6.headline: From PSLE to your first levels
p6.lede: Your PSLE Score sets your Posting Group, and each subject's AL can start it at a more demanding level. Enter ALs to see how it works.

happens.what: Direct School Admission applications, for talents a school recognises.
PSLE written papers. Each subject gets an AL from 1 to 8; the PSLE Score is the sum of four.
Results, the S1 Option Form and the eligibility letter. Six school choices are listed in a short window.
Sec 1 posting results.

decisions.text: With a score of 21 or 22, or 25, choose one of two Posting Groups before listing schools. The choice applies to all six.
List six schools in order. Posting goes by PSLE Score first, then citizenship, choice order and, last, a ballot.
If an AL allows it, decide whether to start English, Mother Tongue, Maths or Science at a more demanding level.

student: Which subject do I enjoy most, whatever my AL?
Would I rather start a subject higher and work hard, or start steady and move up later?
What would I like a secondary school to have: a CCA, a programme, friends, distance from home?
parent: Ask: which subject felt easiest this year, and which felt hardest?
Ask: if you could start one subject at a harder level, which would it be and why?
Ask: what matters to you in a school, beyond the score range?
teacher: Ask the student: what kind of learner are you when something is hard?
Ask: which subject would you be proud to start at a more demanding level?
Ask: who at home will help you decide the six choices?

p6.source: Facts from MOE PSLE and S1 posting pages, read 27 October 2026.

sec1.headline: Settling in, and the first review
sec1.lede: English, Mother Tongue, Maths and Science each sit at G1, G2 or G3. At the end of the year, any of them can move up.

happens.what: A mixed form class for about a third of the week: Art, Music, Design and Technology, Food and Consumer Education, PE and CCE. None of these is levelled.
Levelled subjects are taken with students from other classes at the same level.
The school reviews each levelled subject. English, Mother Tongue, Maths and Science can move up for Sec 2.
Interest and aptitude in Geography, History and Literature this year decide whether they can move up in Sec 2.

decisions.text: Whether to take a subject at a more demanding level next year, if the school offers it. Schools set their own criteria; one common example is 75 percent in the subject at the end of the year.
Which CCA to commit to. It is part of the story every post secondary route reads.

student: Which subject could I move up by the end of the year, and what would my teacher want to see?
Which subject needs more time from me, not a different level?
Is there a Humanities subject I enjoy enough to try harder next year?
parent: Ask: which subject feels like it could go up a level? What would help?
Ask: is any subject taking so much time that the others suffer?
Ask: what does your teacher say you do well?
teacher: Ask the student: which subject would you like to try at the next level?
Ask: what does a good week of revision look like for you?
Ask: which Humanities subject do you look forward to?

sec1.source: Facts from MOE Full SBB FAQ and secondary school experience pages, read 27 October 2026.

sec2.headline: The year that shapes Sec 3
sec2.lede: Humanities can now move too, and at the end of the year your school sets the combination you carry into Sec 3 and Sec 4.

happens.what: Humanities moves up take effect for students who earned them in Sec 1.
Subject combination briefing for upper secondary, at most schools.
Results and school review set your Sec 3 subjects and levels.

decisions.text: Your upper secondary combination: English, Mother Tongue, Maths, a Science option, a Humanities option, and electives. Five to nine exam subjects; seven or eight is typical.
Science: a Science pair, two or three single sciences, or G1 Science.
Humanities: Social Studies with Geography, History or Literature, with single Humanities subjects on top at some schools.
Additional Mathematics, if your school offers it to you. Schools set their own bar, often a Sec 2 G3 Maths mark between 55 and 70 percent.

student: Which subjects do I want in Sec 3 because I like them, not because they sound impressive?
Is there a subject I am one push away from moving up before the combination is set?
Which destinations do I want to keep open, and which subjects hold them?
parent: Ask: which combination would you choose if nobody else had an opinion?
Ask: which subject is one push away from the next level? What would the push look like?
Ask: how many subjects feels right for you: more, or fewer done well?
teacher: Ask the student: which subject in your combination are you choosing for yourself?
Ask: which level would you aim to hold or raise by the end of the year?
Ask: what would make Additional Maths, or a single science, right or wrong for you?

sec2.source: Facts from MOE Full SBB FAQ, read 27 October 2026; combination details from school booklets, provisional.

sec3.headline: Your combination, year one
sec3.lede: The two year SEC course starts. Levels are largely set now; what you do with them is not, and targets start to matter.

happens.what: First year of the SEC course in your combination.
Promotion to Sec 4 and a review where schools can adjust a level, at their discretion.

decisions.text: Set a grade target for each subject. The Targets tab turns them into the scores each destination reads.
Whether any level should change for Sec 4. Up or down is possible but not guaranteed, and depends on the school.

student: Which grade target is a stretch but still mine?
Which subject is costing the most time for the least progress, and why?
Which destination do I want to aim for, and what does it read?
parent: Ask: what grade would you be proud of in each subject?
Ask: which subject needs help that we could find together?
Ask: what are you aiming for after Sec 4, for now?
teacher: Ask the student: which target would you set yourself, before I suggest one?
Ask: what is one habit that would move your weakest grade by one step?
Ask: which destination are you working towards, and do you know what it counts?

sec3.source: Facts from MOE Full SBB pages, read 27 October 2026; review practice varies by school.

sec4.headline: Finishing well, and the SEC
sec4.lede: The first Secondary Education Certificate is sat in 2027. This year is about how you finish, and early admissions can come before the results.

happens.what: Early admissions windows: ITE and polytechnic early admissions, and DSA for JC. Places are offered on aptitude and interest, before the exam.
Orals, listening and science practicals.
English and all Mother Tongue written papers, in one sitting.
All other written papers.
All SEC results together, then the Post Secondary Admissions Exercise opens in mid January.

decisions.text: Whether to apply through an early admissions exercise, and to which course.
Your choices in the Post Secondary Admissions Exercise, the one exercise for JC, MI, polytechnic, PFP and ITE from 2028.
If a fifth year is open to you, whether to take it, and what to aim it at.

student: Which course would I apply for in early admissions, and what would I show them?
Which two grades would move my score the most?
If my results land differently, what is my second road?
parent: Ask: which course would you apply for early, if you could?
Ask: what is your plan if results are better, or worse, than you hope?
Ask: what support would help most between now and October?
teacher: Ask the student: which course are you most curious about, and have you seen it in person?
Ask: which two subjects will you put extra hours into, and when?
Ask: what would you choose if your score came in two points either side?

sec4.source: Facts from SEAB SEC pages and MOE PSE pages, read 27 October 2026.

sec5.headline: A fifth year, aimed at something
sec5.lede: A fifth year paces learning and lets subjects move up a level. It widens what comes next when it is aimed at a destination.

happens.what: Open to students with two or fewer G3 passes who meet a G2 based score: ELMAB3 of 21 or better, or ELB3 or MAB3 of 14 or better, with Grade 5 or better in each subject counted.
Taking every fifth year subject at G3 needs ELMAB3 of 19 or better.
SEC papers again in the subjects taken, then the same Post Secondary Admissions Exercise.

decisions.text: Which subjects to take, and at which level, so the year moves you towards a named destination.
Whether polytechnic through the Foundation Programme or a two year Higher Nitec is a better road than a fifth year, for you.

student: What exactly am I aiming this year at?
Which subject moving to G3 would make the biggest difference?
Would another road get me there sooner, and would I prefer it?
parent: Ask: what do you want this extra year to make possible?
Ask: which subject would you take to G3, and what help do you need?
Ask: have we looked at PFP and Higher Nitec side by side?
teacher: Ask the student: what is the destination this year is for?
Ask: which subject at G3 is realistic for you, and what will change in how you study it?
Ask: what would make you choose a different road instead?

sec5.source: Facts from MOE curriculum page on the SEC and Sec 5, read 27 October 2026.
